preconditions.description: Must be the contract owner to call changeFees() function
Contract must not be in swap state (inSwap == false)

violation_target.exploit_hint: Call changeFees() with parameters that set totalFeeBuy or totalFeeSell to zero, then trigger a transfer that calls takeFeeInProportions() where division by totalFeeBuy or totalFeeSell will occur. Specifically, set reflectionFeeBuy, marketingFeeBuy, and teamFeeBuy all to zero to make totalFeeBuy = 0, or set reflectionFeeSell, marketingFeeSell, and teamFeeSell all to zero to make totalFeeSell = 0. Then execute a buy or sell transaction to trigger the division by zero in the fee calculation.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability exists in the takeFeeInProportions() function where division by totalFeeBuy or totalFeeSell occurs. The contract owner can call changeFees() to set all buy or sell fees to zero, making totalFeeBuy or totalFeeSell zero. When a transfer occurs that triggers fee calculation, the division by zero will revert. The oracle expects totalFeeBuy == 0 || totalFeeSell == 0 to be true, which we can achieve by setting all buy fees to zero.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner to call changeFees() with all buy fees set to zero. 2. Ensure trading is enabled (if needed). 3. Execute a buy transaction (transfer from pair to user) to trigger the division by zero in takeFeeInProportions().
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the owner and call changeFees(0,0,0,2,3,2) to set all buy fees to zero while keeping sell fees non-zero. 2. Enable trading if not already enabled. 3. Transfer tokens from the pair address to another address to simulate a buy transaction, which will trigger the fee calculation with totalFeeBuy = 0.
